common_name: Francis Mason Abelia (Classic Golden-Variegated Glossy Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Francis Mason is a longtime classic golden-variegated abelia and the parent selection behind several newer variegated cultivars.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; more sun produces the brightest gold variegation and the heaviest bloom. Francis Mason is a classic older abelia selection with gold-and-green variegated foliage that takes on bronze-orange tones in cool fall and winter weather, flowering over a long season from late spring into fall with small, fragrant, pale pink, trumpet-shaped blooms that draw butterflies and hummingbirds. Its arching, semi-evergreen habit works well as an informal hedge, foundation planting, or mixed border shrub, and it has served as the parent plant behind several newer, more compact variegated abelia introductions bred for tighter habits. It tolerates heat, humidity, and short dry spells once established, needing only an occasional thinning cut after flowering to control size and remove any all-green reverted shoots, which should be cut out promptly since they grow more vigorously than the variegated growth.

common_name: Sunny Charms Abelia (Low Mounding Chartreuse-Gold Abelia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Sunny Charms stays low and mounded, fitting foundation plantings and border fronts where taller abelia cultivars would need frequent pruning to control size.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; full sun produces the brightest chartreuse-gold foliage color and the heaviest flowering. Sunny Charms forms a naturally low, dense, rounded mound of bright yellow-green foliage that holds its color through the growing season, topped from late spring through fall with small, fragrant, white-to-pale-pink flowers that draw butterflies and hummingbirds. Its compact scale suits low borders, mass plantings, and foundation beds where larger abelia cultivars would need constant cutting back, and it needs little pruning beyond an occasional light shaping after the heaviest bloom flush. It tolerates heat and humidity well once established and is generally trouble-free, making it a low-maintenance option for year-round foliage color in the Gulf South landscape.

common_name: Pugster Periwinkle Butterfly Bush (Dwarf Reblooming Blue-Purple Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Pugster Periwinkle is part of a dwarf, sterile butterfly bush series bred for compact size and continuous rebloom without deadheading.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; good drainage is essential, since butterfly bush is far more likely to be lost to wet winter soil than to cold or drought. Pugster Periwinkle bears dense spikes of blue-purple flowers with a small orange eye on a naturally dwarf, sturdy, well-branched plant, part of the compact, non-invasive Pugster series bred for a tidy habit and continuous bloom from late spring through frost without the need for deadheading. Its low, rounded shape fits foundation plantings, mixed borders, and large containers where the towering size of old-fashioned butterfly bush would overwhelm the space, and its sterile flowers do not set the abundant seed that has made some older Buddleja davidii cultivars invasive in parts of the country. Cut the whole plant back hard in late winter each year, since it flowers on new growth and responds with denser, more floriferous regrowth.

common_name: Dolce Silver Gumdrop Heuchera (Silvery-Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dolce Silver Gumdrop is a Proven Winners introduction with a frosty silver overlay on deep purple leaves and a compact, tidy habit.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; consistent moisture and sharp drainage together matter more to coral bells than either factor alone, since heuchera crowns rot quickly in soggy, poorly drained sites. Dolce Silver Gumdrop bears ruffled, deep purple leaves overlaid with a frosty metallic-silver sheen that catches the light differently than the flatter purple tones of older heuchera cultivars, forming a dense, compact mound well suited to shaded containers and small border plantings. Small, pale flower spikes rise above the foliage in late spring, though the season-long foliage color is the main draw. Provide consistent moisture through summer heat, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the plant vigorous and well-shaped.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Primo Black Pearl Heuchera (Large Near-Black Glossy Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Primo Black Pearl is part of a heuchera breeding line selected for unusually large, substantial leaves and vigorous garden performance.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; good drainage combined with steady moisture keeps the crown from rotting while preventing the plant from drying out in summer heat. Primo Black Pearl produces unusually large, glossy, deeply lobed leaves in a rich near-black purple, part of a Primo breeding line selected for bigger, more substantial foliage and sturdier garden performance than many older, smaller-leaved heuchera cultivars. Its bold scale makes a strong dark accent in mixed shade plantings, especially paired with chartreuse or silver companions for contrast. Small pale flower spikes appear above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the season-long leaf color and texture. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor and prevent the crown from becoming woody and less productive.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens
